answer: An agent marketplace requires each active identity to lock a $100 bond for 30 days before it can bid on jobs. Whether an agent trades under river, dawn, or onyx, its bond stays locked and cannot back another identity during that period. Creating 10,000 fake agents therefore ties up $1 million for a month. This does not prove identities are unique, but it makes scaling a sybil swarm costly by requiring capital for every active account.
